data.body: Debugging observation/hypothesis 2026-09-09: gathered the fresh sunfish CI failure (run 34368820354) and goldeneye history. Sunfish failed on ubuntu py3.13 with '[gw3] node down: Not properly terminated' followed by 'worker gw3 crashed while running tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs'; recheck run 34374220376 passed without code changes. The goldeneye-created observation was different: test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py::test_a_peer_finishing_the_clone_while_we_wait_skips_the_redundant_reclone failed once during full verify but passed alone; on current main the same targeted test passes locally in 2.69s. Deterministic local reproduction found for the sunfish crash class: running test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs with --cov trips pytest-timeout's 3s per-test marker during autouse setup while importing pydantic_ai in tests/conftest.py::_no_live_model_requests. Because timeout_method=thread uses os._exit(1), xdist reports this as a worker crash on the innocent test instead of a Failed: Timeout. Hypothesis under test: this is not OOM and not an xdist provisioning race; it is a too-tight test-local timeout marker covering cold/coverage import setup. Proposed fix is to widen/remove that marker while retaining the test's internal <2s assertion for the actual FastAPI lifespan path, plus a regression guard that forbids this marker from shrinking back below setup headroom.
